text:
GENETIC ENGINEERING
DR. dr. Lailia Nur Rachma, M. Biomed
Microbiology dept. Medical Faculty
Genetic engineering
• The
modification
and
manipulation
of
an
organism's
genes
using
technology

produce
improved
or
novel organisms
• Isolating, copying, inserting, removing, "knock out" genes, transfer of
genes within and across species The new DNA
• The new DNA can be inserted randomly, or targeted to a specific part
of the genome the genetic material of interest using recombinant
DNA methods or by artificially synthesising the DNA Genetically
Modified organism
Genetic engineering
• Is a process that alters the genetic structure of an organism removing or 
introducing DNA, or modifying existing genetic material in situ. 
• Unlike traditional animal and plant breeding involves doing multiple 
crosses and then selecting for the organism with the desired phenotype
• Takes the gene directly from one organism and delivers it to the other 
much faster, could insert any genes from any organism, prevents other 
undesirable genes from also being added.[4]
• Genetic engineering could potentially fix severe genetic disorders in 
humans 
Genetically Modified organism (GMO)
• An
organism
that
is
generated
through
genetic
engineering
(genetically modified)
• The first GMO (1973 ) bacteria Herbert Boyer and Stanley Cohen
• Rudolf Jaenisch (1974) inserted foreign DNA into a mouse
• Genentech (1976) 
Human proteins : human insulin (1978) and
insulin-producing bacteria (1982)

GMOs
• Transgenic : If genetic material from another species is added 
to the host
• Cisgenic : If genetic material from the same species or a 
species that can naturally breed with the host
• Knockout organism : If genetic engineering is used to remove 
genetic material from the target organism
Exclude..
• Traditional breeding
• In vitro fertilization
• Iinduction of polyploidy
• Mutagenesis
• Cell fusion techniques 
• Selective breeding
• Cloning
• Stem cell research
Genetic engineering
• Research
• Medicine
• Industrial Biotechnology 
• Agriculture.
The aims
• To study gene function and expression loss of function, gain of 
function, tracking and expression experiments the function of 
specific could genes to be studied
• By knocking out genes responsible for certain conditions animal 
model organisms of human diseases. 
• Organism producing hormones, vaccines, drugs, enzymes, etc.
• To cure genetic diseases gene therapy replacing the defective 
gene with a functioning one. 
• Agriculture increasing yield, nutritional value and tolerance to 
environmental stresses.
Process Multi-step process
• Choose the gene
• Gene isolation and cloning
• Inserting DNA into the host genome
